On the live board, the section's text renders as the title in its header chip. An optional icon, which can be any glyph, opens the chip, and a section has no detail line. The chip is not a separate object. Give the title and content clear air, and repeat one deliberate gap through each group. A section keeps exactly the geometry it is given. When the region is finished, fit_section closes that one section around the children already inside it and leaves every other section alone. Sections do the grouping: every idea has a home, and each section is an addressable, linkable unit. Nest sections for hierarchy.

A section must not paint the ink or fill of its parent section or of a sibling it touches. A section that holds nodes of several hues must not paint one of them. A category section, whose nodes that are not gray or white all share one hue, can paint that hue. The page (

, or a parentless white section) is the parent of top-level sections. Siblings touch when their edges are closer than one gutter (48px) and part of the gap is clear of other siblings. An agent edit that makes a new break is refused. The

and Studio's duplicate and paste keep the source's color while it keeps the rules. Otherwise the chooser tries gray, blue, violet, green, then teal, and skips the hues of the board's nodes and wires. It keeps a board to three section hues besides gray, category hues included. It does not put teal beside a touching blue or green section while another hue fits. Past that, it repeats the hue of the farthest sibling the section does not touch, a cool hue first. Warm hues come last.
